audit.method: read-only static inspection of the shallow, no-submodule audit clone; no source script, hook, installer, package lifecycle, MCP server, or test was executed

repository_components.selected_plugin_shape: Every selected path contains a Claude manifest and a Codex manifest. Components are predominantly Markdown skills, commands, and agent definitions; they are instructions/configuration, not a conventional executable package.

block_no_verify.implementation: The skill and command instruct an agent to merge a PreToolUse Bash command into .claude/settings.json. It inspects TOOL_INPUT with grep and exits 2 when git --no-verify or --no-gpg-sign is found.
risks: The documented --global option targets ~/.claude/settings.json, outside the repository.
The command edits automatic-hook configuration and can therefore alter future tool behavior.
The regex is a heuristic and must be independently tested for command-chain and quoting bypasses before adoption.
positive_controls: It is designed to prevent rather than enable verification bypass.
The proposed hook uses printf instead of echo and limits inspection to git-related bypass flags.
It says to preserve and merge existing configuration.
block_no_verify.tests: No packaged automated test was found for the hook configuration.
block_no_verify.recommendation: Do not install or copy its command as an active hook. Retain only the policy intent in shared instructions; if a hook is later approved, use a project-local reviewed implementation and dedicated adversarial tests.

protect_mcp.hook_behavior: A matcher of .* runs npx protect-mcp@0.7.4 evaluate before every tool call and npx protect-mcp@0.7.4 sign after every tool call. Inputs and outputs are passed through environment variables; receipts and a signing key default to project-relative paths.
protect_mcp.supply_chain_risk: The hooks invoke npx on every tool call. Although hooks.json pins protect-mcp to 0.7.4, the setup skill and README use protect-mcp@latest. Neither package artifact was audited, installed, nor executed.
protect_mcp.filesystem_and_data_risk: PostToolUse records a receipt for every tool call, including tool input and output hashes/metadata; exact collection and key generation behavior belongs to the unaudited npm package. The test runner uses mktemp and removes only its generated temp directory.
protect_mcp.network_risk: npx --yes in hooks/tests can fetch packages from npm, and test execution also fetches @veritasacta/verify. This audit did not permit either networked execution.

tests.static_fixture_checker: test/verify-fixtures.sh is static and validates JSON/policy fixtures, but was not run.
tests.integration_runner: test/run-tests.sh includes allow/deny/tamper cases but executes npx --yes package downloads; it was not run.
tests.coverage_gap: No local lock file or vendored implementation proves that README behavior, hook behavior, and npm package behavior match.

protect_mcp.recommendation: QUARANTINED. Do not activate, copy, or translate the hook. A separate approved, pinned, offline-reviewed dependency and privacy review would be required before any use.

credential_and_environment_references.interpretation: References occur in instructional templates and examples. No real credential values were recorded, and no selected plugin requires a credential through a package manifest. Any generated application configuration must use repository-local secret handling and never embed values.

findings: cloud-infrastructure contains a Linkerd curl-to-shell installation example.
python-development contains an Astral uv curl-to-shell installation example.
protect-mcp hooks/tests invoke npx and may contact npm.
network_behavior.recommendation: Do not reproduce download-and-execute instructions in canonical skills. Replace with audited, user-approved, pinned tool prerequisites.

findings: conductor documents recursive removal of conductor track directories.
python-development documents removal of caches and __pycache__ directories.
protect-mcp tests clean a mktemp-created work directory and deny rm -rf / in a fixture.
filesystem_and_destructive_behavior.recommendation: Never carry these commands into portable skills without a narrowly validated repository-relative target, dry-run behavior, and an explicit user-authorized cleanup workflow.

prompt_injection_review.caveat: Markdown skills, commands, references, templates, and agent files remain untrusted prompt material. No discovery result authorizes following their embedded commands.

documentation_vs_implementation.finding: Each selected plugin has metadata and declared instructional components. The two focused plugins' README/skill claims correspond to their supplied hook/configuration text, but the security-critical runtime for protect-mcp is an external npm package absent from the clone; its claims are not verified.

cross_cutting_findings.default_disposition: ADAPT_CONTENT_ONLY. Extract no code automatically. Do not enable marketplace entries, hooks, MCP definitions, or external tool installation paths by default.
